dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Systematically mines the contract from tests: reads full common/api-server test files and greps all `use rusternetes_*` imports across crates to reconstruct the required public API surface; understands common→storage→api-server dependency order. Above the 'skim one crate' anchor.
The only engagement with /opt/k8s-reference: ls, find, and a single `cat meta/v1/types.go | head -200` to infer camelCase from json tags. Shallow, and never revisited.

After step 17 the upstream reference is never consulted again; all contract inference is pure test-fitting and compiler-error iteration — matching the 'ignores the upstream reference' clause of the low anchors.

Repeatedly guesses field contracts (ServiceCIDRCondition optionality, observed_generation, IPAddress status field) then corrects them from compile errors rather than from the reference — the 'guesses field names later contradicted by test failures' pattern.
Never mentions or reasons about the hidden conformance suite; contract model is derived entirely from test imports/fixtures, not from source-of-truth k8s v1.35 semantics.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent does substantially more than anchor 3 on the test side — systematic cross-crate import mining, reading full test files, and correct leaf-to-root dependency awareness — but it essentially ignores the upstream reference after a single shallow peek at one types.go (step 17) and repeatedly guesses field contracts that test failures then contradict. It never consults the reference for the specific behaviors each crate is tested on, nor distinguishes fixtures from conformance requirements, so it does not reach anchor 5. This places it at 4: strong test-contract orientation, near-absent reference grounding.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Opening plans state leaf-first ordering explicitly: start with common (shared types), then storage, then api-server 'and others' — dependency-aware sequencing intent from the outset.

Gated common on its own tests passing (34 tests) before moving to storage, then storage compiles before api-server — the level-5 'compiles + its tests pass' per-crate milestone check applied to the first two layers.

Repeated intent to count tests per crate and 'implement api-server first (largest), then controller-manager, then others' — prioritization by payoff on top of DAG order, slightly above pure level 5, but no concrete per-crate exit criteria or sub-milestones written down.

Mid-run the layered discipline collapses: 'fixing each error is too slow', so it mass-generates controller-manager (23 controllers), scheduler, kubectl, kubelet, kube-proxy, cloud-providers all at once via Python scripts — an undifferentiated push with no milestone gating for downstream crates.

Downstream crates never individually verified before Submit; api-server tests still fail to compile. No sub-milestone decomposition of the large api-server crate (types→wiring→handlers→watches) ever materialized.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server) and uses 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check for the first layers, matching the level-5 anchor; it adds mild test-count prioritization intent. However it never reaches level 8: there is no explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with per-crate exit criteria or sub-milestones inside large crates, and no maintained milestone artifact. Mid-run it abandons the layered gating entirely to mass-generate all downstream crates at once, so sustained milestone discipline is absent across the full horizon, holding the score at 5.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Early, genuine verify loop on the leaf common crate: repeated `cargo test -p rusternetes-common`, diagnosing compile errors and confirming 34 tests pass before moving on.

Periodic workspace-wide verification with `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` interleaved with per-crate builds/checks; used grep on `error[`/`test result` to gauge state — solid but treats a green provided suite as the only bar.

Tracks per-crate provided-test counts (api-server 813, controller-manager 181, kubectl 168, etc.) and runs `--no-run` compile checks per crate; verification is real but often reduced to compile-error triage since tests barely compiled.

Final workspace test run attempts hampered by timeouts; agent marks task complete with api-server tests still failing to compile. No use of prescribed --test-threads/skip-list, and never any reasoning about the hidden HTTP conformance suite or booting the all-in-one binary.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and runs the workspace suite periodically (anchor 5), and even tracks per-crate counts. However, it never reasons about the hidden conformance suite, HTTP/JSON semantics, or booting the all-in-one binary, and never used the prescribed thread/skip settings — the defining features of anchor 8 are absent. Much of its 'verification' degraded into grepping compile errors rather than pass/fail triage, keeping it at a solid anchor-5 level.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Established and repeatedly refreshed a per-crate test census: ~1279 tests across ~95 files, then a concrete breakdown (api-server 813, controller-manager 181, kubectl 168, kubelet 64, scheduler 19, common 34). This is a genuine horizon tally, above a merely qualitative sense.

Consistently tracked the one verified number it had ('common passes 34 tests') and which crates were stubs vs compiling, and re-ran cargo test/check to reconfirm. But it never obtained real pass counts for any crate beyond common — everything else stayed at 'fails to compile,' so its ledger of actual passes never grew past 34.

Long circular episode: the Secret struct / duplicate normalize was broken, re-diagnosed, and re-fixed across ~20 steps (orphaned braces, accidental full removal of Secret, re-adding). It noticed the stuck state each time but never named the loop or changed strategy to escape it efficiently — evidence of thrashing on one file within an already-green crate.

At step 159 it declared 'implemented all missing source files for all 10 crates,' mistaking code volume for verified progress; steps 161-165 then revealed api-server (813 tests) wouldn't even compile. It marked the task complete while the true state was 34 verified passes. The final analysis (step 165) is, however, an accurate honest accounting of the real state.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-3 'rough qualitative' anchor: it built and repeatedly refreshed a per-crate test-count census and tracked which crates compiled vs. remained stubs, and it noticed stuck states (the Secret duplication). That matches the level-5 anchor ('tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much is green; notices when a crate is stuck'). It falls short of level 8 because it never maintained a concrete ledger of pass counts per binary (only common's 34 was ever a verified figure), it thrashed on the same file across ~20 steps without naming the loop, and at the end it mistook 'wrote source for all crates' for global progress despite tests never compiling — the exact failure mode the higher anchors warn against.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Test evidence showed IPAddress must not carry a status field and ServiceCIDRCondition needed different field types; agent revised the structs to match rather than forcing the original design.
storage crate's async_channel dependency was unavailable; agent switched to tokio broadcast and dropped the watch approach when it proved blocking — a real approach change from build evidence.

Recognized the inferred Arc<dyn Storage> contract was wrong (E0038 not dyn-compatible), checked that tests actually use Arc<MemoryStorage>, and reworked to generic Storage parameters — an approach-level reversal citing test evidence (anchor-8 flavor).
Repeated local Python 'remove orphaned brace' fixes on resources.rs — patch-the-symptom thrashing rather than reconsidering the code-generation method that produced the corruption.

At the end, agent enumerated multiple falsified contracts (Pod::new signature, ConfigMap binary_data type, missing HasMetadata impls) but left them uncorrected and marked complete; no re-verification of downstream crates after the bulk generation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent went well beyond pure local patching: it twice recognized that a whole inferred approach/contract was wrong (dyn Storage → generics; async_channel/watch → tokio/removed) and reworked it while citing the test/build evidence that triggered the change, which is above the anchor-5 'update the signature' level. However, the trajectory also contains substantial patch-the-error thrashing (repeated brace-removal cycles) and ends with several recognized-but-uncorrected falsified assumptions and no downstream re-verification, so it falls short of the fluid, systemic, cost-avoiding adaptation of anchor 8-10. This places it at a 6, between the 5 and 8 descriptions.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
